| | | Listen. There’s a lot of anxiety about this election, and for good reason. I feel it too. So before the next three weeks swallow us whole, let’s take a breath and spend one minute on something ridiculous. At a rally in Tennessee on Saturday, the President announced that he thinks an ocean should be named after him. An ocean. “Trump Ocean,” he suggested, or “Ocean of the Americas, something like that.” He’d also like a river, though he ruled out the Hudson and the Mississippi. This comes after the Gulf of America, after an order telling federal agencies to call Lake Ontario “Lake America,” and after he floated “New America” for New Mexico. Canada’s prime minister says Canadians will keep calling it Lake Ontario “then, now and always.” I’m told he was joking. Then again, as he put it on Saturday, “Everyone thinks I kid.” There’s only one name change I’m interested in this year: Which party is in control of Congress and the Senate. Right now, Congress is run by Republicans who have let Trump do whatever he wants while prices climb and a war drags on. In 18 days, voters get to change that. Republican-controlled becomes Democratic-controlled. That’s the only renaming project I’m working on. clean_body: | | | | = | | | Listen. There’s a lot of anxiety about this election, and for good reason. I feel it too. So before the next three weeks swallow us whole, let’s take a breath and spend one minute on something ridiculous. At a rally in Tennessee on Saturday, the President announced that he thinks an ocean should be named after him. An ocean. “Trump Ocean,” he suggested, or “Ocean of the Americas, something like that.” He’d also like a river, though he ruled out the Hudson and the Mississippi. This comes after the Gulf of America, after an order telling federal agencies to call Lake Ontario “Lake America,” and after he floated “New America” for New Mexico. Canada’s prime minister says Canadians will keep calling it Lake Ontario “then, now and always.” I’m told he was joking. Then again, as he put it on Saturday, “Everyone thinks I kid.” There’s only one name change I’m interested in this year: Which party is in control of Congress and the Senate. Right now, Congress is run by Republicans who have let Trump do whatever he wants while prices climb and a war drags on. In 18 days, voters get to change that. name: Congressman Vince Fong
subject: Fighting for Affordability
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Vince Fong for Congress
body:
Something I am hearing every day in California: the cost of living is crushing families here. | | |
---
| |
# Fighting for Affordability
---
| Friend, Something I am hearing every day in California: the cost of living is crushing families here. Ask anyone in our district what worries them most, and the high cost of living tops the list. I’ve been fighting for more affordability in California since my first day in Sacramento and I’ve continued that fight in Washington, DC. Back [in 2020, when I introduced legislation to cut taxes](https://us.list-manage.com/RQ2K0USwqs4?e=affd398937&c2id=4fd8e839bd16eef39626cb246bcc01d8) for middle class families, small businesses, and renters, I said plainly: _"The cost of living in California is driving out so many families to other states because they cannot bear this burden any longer."_ That same year, [I called out Sacramento](https://us.list-manage.com/dgz8DHQ6cMy?e=affd398937&c2id=4fd8e839bd16eef39626cb246bcc01d8) for quietly hiking the gas tax by another $440 million without so much as a vote of the Legislature or the public. By [2022, with inflation hammering household budgets](https://us.list-manage.com/wKMqTXin7Ps?e=affd398937&c2id=4fd8e839bd16eef39626cb246bcc01d8) and gas topping $5.70 a gallon in parts of our state, I was back at it again, introducing legislation to suspend the state gas tax outright. Something is wrong in California when the average price of gasoline in our state is $6.21 and the average price in Indiana is $3.89. We know one of the first things our out of state friends do while visiting is they take a photo of California’s gas prices. I've been fighting this fight since I first got to the State Assembly in 2016, long before affordability became the issue everyone's suddenly talking about. It's why I've spent my time in Congress fighting Sacramento's hidden climate tax on shipping that drives up prices at the register and the pump. It's why I fought to pull the plug on California's $128 billion high-speed rail boondoggle instead of letting it drain resources from roads and water systems that actually serve our families. It's why I'm fighting the State Water Board every time it tries to raise costs and uncertainty for the farmers who feed this country. It’s why I am working to expand oil and gas production in our community, to invest in California’s energy pipeline infrastructure, and to actually build and expand refining capacity to support increase supplies of needed gasoline, diesel and jet fuel. I will continue to work every single day to tackle the affordability crisis in California. Let’s invest in water infrastructure to increase needed water supplies for our homes, businesses and farms. Let’s increase California’s gasoline and diesel supplies to lower prices at the pump. Let’s get rid of red tape and bureaucracy that is making everything more expensive. And let’s reduce your tax burden so you keep more of your hard earned money. Thank you for standing with me,
Congressman Vince Fong

He's working tirelessly to create jobs, cut taxes, and make Ohio the best place to learn and start a business. He's made it his mission to defend the rights of women, children, and the unborn. And he's fighting to ensure that everyone-even the underdogs, the outsiders, and the voiceless-can achieve their own version of the American Dream. But Jon can't win this fight alone. | | We're building the movement for a better America, and we need your skin in the game to help us win big! | | Paid for by Husted for Senate P.O. body:
Central New Yorkers are fighters. Here’s what I told him.

| | | | |

Peter,

This past week, I shared the stage at President Trump’s rally in Syracuse...
I’m still fired up!
_And because you’ve been with this campaign from the start, I want to share what I told him at the rally._
**I told him Central New Yorkers are FIGHTERS.**
We are not going to sit back while John Mannion and the Democrats raise our taxes, drive up our energy bills, and then ask our families to just live with it.
And we are NOT going to let liberal mega-donors buy this seat on Election Day.
---
| [JOIN ME NOW >>](https://us.list-manage.com/_IwfSubG8Wp?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)

**So when the so-called experts call this a “tough race,” here’s my answer: that doesn’t scare me one bit.**
People all across Central New York are stepping up in a huge way. And every time they do, this race gets closer.
**President Trump said it himself: “You’re right there. You’re gonna win that sucker.”**
He’s right. We are within striking distance, and we are NOT going down without a fight.
**But we’re running out of time. Early voting starts October 24th. Election Day is November 3rd.**
That’s just weeks to reach every voter in NY-22 before the Democrats and their mega-donors drown out our message.
Will you chip in $25 right now to help me finish the job?

subject: The richest people on Earth are pouring trillions into AI. We must fight back.

body:
|

Peter, it's Bernie Sanders. [**_In just a moment, I will ask for your financial support to help elect progressive leaders to Congress._**](https://act.weareprogressives.org/go/106450?t=9&refcode=EM_ALL_CPC_FR_6_2026-10-16_BER_AIG_ES-64357&amount=26&akid=28345%2E3658908%2Ee8ISv_) But first, I want to talk to you about something that I believe is one of the most important issues facing our country. Artificial intelligence is on the brink of becoming the most transformational technology in the history of the world, and will profoundly affect the life of everyone in this country. It will bring unprecedented change to our economy, our democracy, our mental well‐being, and how we raise our children. There is even a possibility, and research that supports it, that as AI becomes smarter than humans, it could eventually function independently, with potentially catastrophic consequences. The question is not whether AI will change the world. We are already watching it happen. **The question, the only question that matters right now, is who will own and control that future.** Right now, the answer to all of those questions is the same small group of people. A handful of Big Tech oligarchs (Elon Musk, Sam Altman, Jeff Bezos, Mark Zuckerberg, Larry Ellison) are moving as fast as they possibly can to make sure all of it works for them, not for you. AI and automation could eliminate nearly 100 million American jobs over the next decade. Musk himself said, "AI and robots will replace all jobs." Technology that does not take a salary, need a vacation, require healthcare, or form a union makes them and their corporate clients far richer and more powerful. We have been here before. In the 1990s, working people were told that free trade would create millions of new jobs and raise wages. That was a lie. The real goal was to shut down American factories and greatly enhance profits for large corporations. Now the same class of billionaires is making the same promises about AI. We know how that story ends. But right now, we have a chance to write a different ending. We must elect progressive leaders who will regulate AI, stand up to Big Tech oligarchs and fight for working people. The Ninth Circuit held that the law violated the National Voter Registration Act (“NVRA”). The U.S. Supreme Court agreed to hear the case in June, and oral argument is scheduled for December 8, 2026.Our brief argues that under the Voter Qualifications Clause of the Constitution, states have sole authority to establish and verify voter qualifications, including citizenship, and that Congress cannot use its power under the Elections Clause and the NVRA to override that authority in state elections. Voter registration is more than an administrative process – it allows election officials to determine whether applicants meet eligibility requirements before Election Day:
> Congress cannot usurp the state’s exclusive sovereign prerogative to adjudicate whether an applicant has presented satisfactory proof of those qualifications, such as residency or citizenship ...
The brief explains that voter registration helps ensure that only qualified voters can vote and allows officials to verify eligibility before Election Day. It argues that when a state requires advance registration, it should be able to decide what proof is needed to establish that an applicant meets the state’s constitutional voting qualifications:
> Before Election Day, state election officials verify qualifications so that on Election Day voting can proceed efficiently with limited challenges.***Like all states, Arizona requires individuals to be citizens of the United States to be qualified to vote in its state and federal elections. Pursuant to its authority under the Constitution’s Voter Qualifications Clause, it mandates registrants to provide proof of their citizenship to vote in state elections.
The brief warns that allowing federal procedural regulation to prevent states from enforcing their own voter qualifications would upset the constitutional division of authority between the federal government and the states.The Left is desperately opposed, contrary to law, to make it as easy as possible for foreign nationals to illegally vote in our elections. **Judicial Watch Sues for Abdul El-Sayed Animal Euthanasia Records **Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Michigan, served as executive director and health officer of the Detroit Health Department in Detroit from 2015 until 2017. Peter, Roy Cooper here. I’m worried.
We’re 17 days out from the election, and in-person early voting has already started here in North Carolina. Our fundraising is not where it needs to be this close to Election Day. [**_If you’re able to chip in today for the first time to help us get back on track, it would make a big impact and mean a lot to me._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1692&amount=5&t=9&akid=4616%2E124072%2E3P3HHd)
Here’s why it’s so important that we see a surge in grassroots donations today:
North Carolina is where the fight for U.S. Senate control will be won or lost. Flipping this seat is a _must_ if we’re going to take back the majority, and that’s why the GOP is going all in to defeat me.
Republican super PACs have flooded this race with tens of millions to crush our momentum. President Trump has smeared my name to his millions of followers on social media. **He’s even coming to North Carolina _next week_ to hold a rally with my MAGA opponent.**
**If folks like you chip in and we hit our fundraising goals, we’ll be able to keep up with the GOP and ensure this race stays competitive. If we don’t meet this goal, we won’t.**
[**_That’s why this is so important, Peter, so I have to ask: Will you give $5 or whatever amount you can spare today to help us reach our goal, flip North Carolina and take back the Senate majority?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1692&amount=5&t=10&akid=4616%2E124072%2E3P3HHd)

name: Lieutenant Colonel Alex Vindman, US Army, Retired
subject: The Washington Post
body:
Peter: A little more than six years ago, I retired from active military service.
I had no intention to resign from a career I loved, having served for more than 21 years in uniform. But it became clear that Donald Trump had a vendetta against me, and that he would do everything in his power to punish me for speaking truth to power.
On that first day of retirement, I wrote an article in _The Washington Post_ discussing the need to have public servants with the moral courage to protect our democracy. This is more relevant than ever.
I’ve attached the op-ed below. It's an important reminder of why doing what's right matters. Thank you for taking a few minutes to read it.
Before you go, please make a donation to my brother Eugene's re-election to Congress. He won one of the closest races in the country last cycle and needs our help to do it again. Every donation to his campaign - no matter the size - helps.
**[DONATE](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/evfc-em-oct26?refcode=em261017-av&refcode2=1163_3892029_lxMJhp&akid=1163%2E3892029%2ElxMJhp)**
* * *

[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/evfc-em-oct26?refcode=em261017-av&refcode2=1163_3892029_lxMJhp&akid=1163%2E3892029%2ElxMJhp)
**Alexander Vindman: Coming forward ended my career. I still believe doing what’s right matters.**
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/evfc-em-oct26?refcode=em261017-av&refcode2=1163_3892029_lxMJhp&akid=1163%2E3892029%2ElxMJhp)
After 21 years, six months and 10 days of active military service, I am now a civilian. I made the difficult decision to retire because a campaign of bullying, intimidation and retaliation by President Trump and his allies forever limited the progression of my military career.
This experience has been painful, but I am not alone in this ignominious fate. The circumstances of my departure might have been more public, yet they are little different from those of dozens of other lifelong public servants who have left this administration with their integrity intact but their careers irreparably harmed.
A year ago, having served the nation in uniform in positions of critical importance, I was on the cusp of a career-topping promotion to colonel. A year ago, unknown to me, my concerns over the president’s conduct and the president’s efforts to undermine the very foundations of our democracy were precipitating tremors that would ultimately shake loose the facade of good governance and publicly expose the corruption of the Trump administration.
At no point in my career or life have I felt our nation’s values under greater threat and in more peril than at this moment. Our national government during the past few years has been more reminiscent of the authoritarian regime my family fled more than 40 years ago than the country I have devoted my life to serving.
Our citizens are being subjected to the same kinds of attacks tyrants launch against their critics and political opponents. Those who choose loyalty to American values and allegiance to the Constitution over devotion to a mendacious president and his enablers are punished. The president recklessly downplayed the threat of the pandemic even as it swept through our country. The economic collapse that followed highlighted the growing income disparities in our society. Millions are grieving the loss of loved ones and many more have lost their livelihoods while the president publicly bemoans his approval ratings.
There is another way.
During my testimony in the House impeachment inquiry, I reassured my father, who experienced Soviet authoritarianism firsthand, saying, “Do not worry, I will be fine for telling the truth.” Despite Trump’s retaliation, I stand by that conviction. Even as I experience the low of ending my military career, I have also experienced the loving support of tens of thousands of Americans. Theirs is a chorus of hope that drowns out the spurious attacks of a disreputable man and his sycophants.
Since the struggle for our nation’s independence, America has been a union of purpose: a union born from the belief that although each individual is the pilot of their own destiny, when we come together, we change the world. We are stronger as a woven rope than as unbound threads.
America has thrived because citizens have been willing to contribute their voices and shed their blood to challenge injustice and protect the nation. It is in keeping with that history of service that, at this moment, I feel the burden to advocate for my values and an enormous urgency to act.
Despite some personal turmoil, I remain hopeful for the future for both my family and for our nation. Impeachment exposed Trump’s corruption, but the confluence of a pandemic, a financial crisis and the stoking of societal divisions has roused the soul of the American people. A groundswell is building that will issue a mandate to reject hate and bigotry and a return to the ideals that set the United States apart from the rest of the world. I look forward to contributing to that effort.
In retirement from the Army, I will continue to defend my nation. I will demand accountability of our leadership and call for leaders of moral courage and public servants of integrity. I will speak about the attacks on our national security. I will advocate for policies and strategies that will keep our nation safe and strong against internal and external threats. I will promote public service and exalt the contribution that service brings to all areas of society.
The 23-year-old me who was commissioned in December 1998 could never have imagined the opportunities and experiences I have had. I joined the military to serve the country that sheltered my family’s escape from authoritarianism, and yet the privilege has been all mine.
When I was asked why I had the confidence to tell my father not to worry about my testimony, my response was, “Congressman, because this is America. This is the country I have served and defended, that all my brothers have served, and here, right matters.”
To this day, despite everything that has happened, I continue to believe in the American Dream. I believe that in America, right matters. I want to help ensure that right matters for all Americans.

👋 Wait! Before you scroll away...🇺🇸
My brother Eugene won one of the closest House races in the country last cycle, and that makes him a big time target for Republicans who want to keep control of the House, and a president who'd love to defeat the second Vindman twin.
Eugene has some final spending decisions to make in the next few days and he can use your help to fully-fund his get out the vote program. This is a big deal.
He tells me that he's a bit short of where he needs to be right now, so I was hoping people who care about holding the House could help.
**If $15 seems worth it to you to take back the House majority, then I am asking: Please contribute to my brother Eugene Vindman’s campaign today.**
**[DONATE](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/evfc-em-oct26?refcode=em261017-av&refcode2=1163_3892029_lxMJhp&akid=1163%2E3892029%2ElxMJhp)**

Paid for by the Alex Vindman Victory Fund, a joint fundraising committee authorized by Alex Vindman for Florida, the Democratic Executive Committee of Florida and the DSCC.
4611 S University Drive #194
Davie, FL 33328
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Small-dollar donations from people like you are the primary way Alex Vindman funds this campaign — if you would like to make a contribution, you can do so by [clicking this link](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/avvf-digi-em-q32026?refcode=em_footer&t=1&refcode2=1163_3892029_lxMJhp&akid=1163%2E3892029%2ElxMJhp).
Email is a very important way we communicate with supporters like you. If you would like to recieve fewer emails, [sign up here](https://act.alexvindman.com/signup/avfl_feweremails/?t=2&akid=1163%2E3892029%2ElxMJhp) or if you must, you can [unsubscribe here](https://act.alexvindman.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=3&akid=1163%2E3892029%2ElxMJhp).
Alexander Vindman is a former member of the United States Army. Use of his military rank, job titles, and photographs in uniform does not imply endorsement by the U.S. Army, the Department of Defense or any branch of the U.S. government.

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Abbott’s campaign is sinking
body:
We turned a long shot into a dead heat. Now we need to finish it.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
**Two new polls just came out showing me ahead of Greg Abbott by 1-2 points.**
That’s the fifth and sixth poll in the last month to show us leading this race. Not tied. Ahead.
If you’d told me a year ago, when we launched this campaign, that we’d be here, I’m not sure I would have believed you. But here we are, and it’s because of people like you.
**[So I’m asking: will you make](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261017_1_poll.6IG0U1&refcode=em20261017-2455&amount=5&t=1&akid=2455%2E299639%2EhWWOJF)[your first-ever donation of $15 today to keep this momentum going?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261017_1_poll.6IG0U1&refcode=em20261017-2455&amount=15&t=2&akid=2455%2E299639%2EhWWOJF)**
Here’s what the numbers tell me:
Texans know Greg Abbott, and they’re tired of him. 52% of likely voters view him unfavorably, and only 44% favorably. **After more than a decade of corruption that’s left Texas families to fend for themselves, voters across the political spectrum are ready for change.**
And the more Texans get to know me, the more they like what they see. My name ID has jumped to 79% in just the last few weeks, and I’m still viewed favorably by a 12-point margin (45% to 33%), even after Abbott has spent millions attacking me.
Grassroots donations from this team made that possible. **[Will you make your first contribution so we can reach the voters who still don’t know me?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261017_1_poll.6IG0U1&refcode=em20261017-2455&amount=5&t=4&akid=2455%2E299639%2EhWWOJF)**
Together, we’ve turned this race from a long shot into a dead heat. A few months ago, people said we’d never get this close to taking Texas back. Now we’re on the edge of making history.
But Abbott knows it too. He’s raised more than $141 million in this campaign and already spent over $120 million of it trying to stop us. He still has $17 million left to spend on false attack ads right as voting begins. **The undecided voters who will decide this race are about to be buried in them, and we need to make sure they hear from us too.**
If you’ve been meaning to give, now is the time. **[Can you make your first gift before early voting starts so we can stay on the air in the final weeks?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261017_1_poll.6IG0U1&refcode=em20261017-2455&amount=5&t=6&akid=2455%2E299639%2EhWWOJF)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261017_1_poll.6IG0U1&amount=5&refcode=em20261017-2455&t=25&akid=2455%2E299639%2EhWWOJF)
Thank you,
Gina

Peter,

If you’ve been keeping an eye on the fight to retake a Democratic majority
in the Senate, you probably already know that competitive seats in states
like Maine, Texas, and Alaska are currently in play for Democrats. That is
massively exciting news.

But as much as I want Democrats to win those races, we have to be
realistic about the math. The fact of the matter is that Republicans only
need to flip Michigan in order to hold onto their majority.

If they flip this seat in Michigan, our chances at winning the Senate are
toast.

I don’t say all this to scare you, but I want to be honest about what this
means for our race:

* Republicans have made me their #1 target to beat in November, and they
are dropping $1 million a day on ads from now until Election Day.

* That means the hundreds of thousands of Michiganders who are currently
choosing whether to vote for me, Mike Rogers, or whether to even vote
at all are being swamped with attack ads in this final push.

The window to make a difference in the outcome of this race is closing
fast, so if you’ve been waiting for the right moment to make your first
contribution to our campaign, this is it. [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261017-1-ak.V6W2-H&amount=10&refcode=em20261017-3586&t=1005&akid=3600%2E251025%2EgaQuc3 ]Will you please donate

# 5 Days Until Early Vote.
Friends,
We have run with everything we had and we are not done. We are running to win and through the finish line.

"You've run an amazing race!" "You're almost there for the win - keep it up!" Those are the words of encouragement we are hearing all over Maryland.

But we have a task to finish - we need a final TV ad buy and we need your help to do it. To date, we've raised and spent over a quarter-million fighting for you.

_**Now we need a final $50,000 to finish the TV ad buy with a new ad for the final election weeks.**_

[$1776 gives us 10 spots on cable tv. $176 gives us one spot](https://us.list-manage.com/nUSNBb21AyA?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b). Thank you and now it's time to vote - let's win together for our families, our children and for all of Maryland.

For Maryland,

Dan Cox
Next Governor of Maryland

Take our poll below and let us know what you think. Some of the most trusted drinks in your fridge have a health reputation they never earned. That reputation shapes what you pour at breakfast, grab after a workout, and hand to your kids, yet most people don't check the label. ## Trump Calls Zelensky a 'Disgrace'
President Trump called Ukraine's renewed strikes on Russian oil refineries [a disgrace](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMFuhCAYhJ9GbxhARHvg0Iu37bVH86_87P4VYQOsxj5946Z9gh5nJpnMN5-X6QLkKdw-YEVTXJwC7tljKZimkp7rY8vf6DHk5SiYPWTnD5okl5oJzkQ_wVxow0lBbY1DlNjWaET_JmUrVNfXd-OuILhWqGe4DrLtB8F76xTXWkiQbqjJnH2Ci15wroRukKtOzd1gO6u5aFWlOFoqMTVfkUK5o_NH3DA1c1xrb-6lPHLVvldyrOS473sTrvPJceanE5O3lRyfSwIKWMnxRcZ-Ncsl0YKZpWfOBIFF8sxSviWYkf3RHywXSJ7CwtIcQPN2UEOdjH3s5D1l3VeK31Yg_1pV_nnmZuRPAAAA__-JGozf), saying Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky was harder to deal with than Russian President Vladimir Putin. Kyiv [resumed the strikes](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOnDAQQL8GOq9sr8FQuEiz3aVNiSZ4fDtZY688A4h8fXT5heufnp7er4_lAyhT-fwJGwZJdSl4ckYRbIu0fXsf_BczFn5dgpyBU75osdqOymhl_AKr0IGLgz6GhGjx3mMwfrb2btzg-2eYoh_NOP3GYZ4HgCGNU5y1jej9Oq0JegpfPqONN1o7M95Qu8GtwxSHOGpzd53TGElqu_2pVOSJKV_1wHZb69bn8BR5c3f_0dlHZx_ned42yiTQri-gs4_91YAKqoa8b8gKRGB9sapFtZ2ZoKhKWTVMVLARsqop0UqQWTFcCljtrBpmEKqFlSAKtr6F-D4pZ-LRd05_bkD5f5J88-QR7L8AAAD__xdmjZw) against Russian energy sites after Zelensky said the U.S. had cut intelligence sharing and throttled Starlink satellite communications, declaring he was "done" with the energy ceasefire Trump announced last week. Zelensky said Russia never stopped hitting Ukraine's grid, launching more than 850 drones since midnight Thursday despite the truce. Trump announced the ceasefire Sunday, saying an end to strikes on energy sites would ease pressure on fuel supplies. Zelensky spent Friday in Brussels, where [EU leaders rallied](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkTHO2zAMhU8jbwokRrbrwUMXb3_XjgZr0QkbRgpEOYZ7-sJBb9CF4PBA4vvez6_5C1k43X7gk8a65jnRrkK1Uplr2Z6vt_4hoaSPo5IK6ioHz-Cgs95Z38-4VH7THLCJ40oEdG1o9P0AcPWh7Zv7uA4BA1DEGKFFCriuXRji4j0F6PpfDY_nPe98750LvruQC21Y2m-xjZ3z12CCo8g1l8vvzKneaZUjv6lclvxsZLzX-lJz_W5gMjDt-37ZFGuOeJwBA5PWXA4D08l2JnKRaGA6vxqYvDvHudFmhTBSUVtQ5LBY8pai_WeAD4tqP1bsgiJqt0dBTozJai38ILU52bKpMlq0kfVWcCED0wDQD24IzvUGpqaM8bWzCGvXm-BuT2T5wNT_7OA9wt8AAAD__yrcnRM) around him and looked for ways to give new assistance to Ukraine.
## White House Press Secretary To Exit
Katie Zacharia is [out as White House press secretary](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAUhJ8Gd1iAwTgFxTbusu2WFoHj-Gzwj-DElvP0V84r3G6kkWb0ff_uw91jwuX518_gaFyHBY6SgAjyQPk9b3v5QIKlvE6CknwZ04mDEqrlUnBpBx8Idxi0r6IbARQ0FThpb0o1UhtbTc6qIKxqrBHdw_qbeBiQsWuMlmMXg5EVumtPCmmlEFq2NQhtdDBdNLEVstFMC4hIa67_r7jQBGM61x1yHda5Sm4i2gpr_jDVM9Ufx1GHR7k4rp6p_opM9V8c_vKEwD8-TD6j58eEBHxa3wX4lqEUXiBkIJ9Ppvoqu7gdmBKW1jItnrPH9H2lX8ranfoJAAD__yAYgLg) one week to the day after President Trump named her, capping days of controversy over her performance and her claims of being a lawyer. A senior White House official told Fox News she is ["transitioning out."](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1yhCAUBeCn0Q4HEP8KijR2mzalw8J1JYvicK8S8_SZ3VdIfWbOnO983aab8cFvj0-zgqY5ThtkDEAEaaJ0rPuJvxBgw-dFgMHgHC4_SS5bJjgT3WQs-RMmZUqnZwAJdQladIOUtVBNVy5atIPlQ8_7u5WdVa5XICxvpG36noMbSq9ffYKLTnCuRFsBV42yTe8a13JRq0JxcJ5iqr6j32iBOVzxhFTZuJZBL0Q7FvVHIcdCjjnnao4_L8crL-S4x-DJWyzk-CYxa5CQuXjciW2Q2Z4AkSHYBGTShWw-6EjAzEyQWIr2ebG8eAK2xAOBObgfVCbt9uxD8Nh2heKP1fjwXkT_PPLU8i8AAP__viuMhw) Trump denied firing her Friday, saying the press had "brutalized" her and that he advised her to reconsider the job. Her [first press conference (see video)](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFyqzAQheGnEZ2Z3WWFcKHiNnS-bUpGRitbiUAepECcp884r5D6zHwz53-7TBcXU1xv_90itoY8rXKUJLXKNtXtc3ns5VuSrOXjWaUkV0J6xomA-hPCCc3k5hp3mdg13gYRkq4Ri-ZM1CFr09xtd3VahM4eDenZ45V5HgwGmkG7wfsm2peHgAYBGPtWgDXPevDa94AdKwbxseatfc9xrXcJ6Zl32do5L02y91ofRXX_FI2KxuM42pC_Xj9eu6Jxj16yorFn6I3mMwyI1GzWP46YUiy9UQy3xcX0C9Y_dtgt_QQAAP__LNBxPQ) on Tuesday was heavily criticized amid growing questions over over her legal credentials. She acknowledged this week that she never passed the bar exam.

Dear Peter, **I believe Mainers deserve a Governor who answers only to them** and who understands how hard it has become to afford life here in Maine. I am determined to be that leader.

With Election Day approaching, I want to make sure more Mainers know they have that choice. And I'm asking you to help me reach them.

**Would you consider making your first contribution of $25 today?**

Your gift will help us reach voters directly through texts, social media and emails in these final weeks, when so many Mainers are deciding who deserves their vote.
---
| [](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/donate?e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=10_17_a&n=1 "Chip in $25") [Chip in $25](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/donate?e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=10_17_a&n=1)
---
There's another reason I'm asking today. **Tuesday, October 20 is our final campaign finance reporting deadline before Election Day.** That report will be public, and it will show Mainers who is standing behind this campaign.

We haven't taken a penny of party money or dark money. We've made it this far because people who care about Maine have decided to invest in something different.

Your first contribution, whatever the amount, **will help us finish this campaign the same way we started it: independent, accountable, and answering only to Mainers.**

I'm grateful you're considering being part of it. Rick Bennett

In just a few hours, Trump is taking the stage in Kentucky in a last-ditch attempt to save Andy Barr's campaign.
On the surface, this may not seem like great news.
But for a campaign like mine, where nobody thought I could make it this far, I'm beaming: Andy has no choice but to call in his boss because he can't win alone.
The establishment never thought a Democrat could tie in the polls with a Republican in _Kentucky_ of all places.
One hard truth has defined this race: no matter your background or party affiliation, our rigged political system has repeatedly failed working-class families across our Commonwealth.
Fixing our broken system doesn't come from electing a copy-and-paste version of the people in charge, who've wrecked us in the first place.
**It comes from a leader who understands the struggle on a personal level and is willing to stand up to the corruption that allows it to persist. I hope to be that leader for you.**
Before Andy and Trump take the stage, will you chip in $25 to prove that our grassroots movement alone is enough to carry us to the finish line?

But for a campaign like mine, where nobody thought I could make it this far, I'm beaming: Andy has no choice but to call in his boss because he can't win alone. The establishment never thought a Democrat could tie in the polls with a Republican in Kentucky of all places. One hard truth has defined this race: no matter your background or party affiliation, our rigged political system has repeatedly failed working-class families across our Commonwealth. Fixing our broken system doesn't come from electing a copy-and-paste version of the people in charge, who've wrecked us in the first place. It comes from a leader who understands the struggle on a personal level and is willing to stand up to the corruption that allows it to persist. I hope to be that leader for you. Before Andy and Trump take the stage, will you chip in $25 to prove that our grassroots movement alone is enough to carry us to the finish line? Thank you. Our volunteer student canvassers have been through the wringer these past couple of months.

This sponsored message from Inside Scoop Politics is on behalf of Hillsdale College

| | Dear Fellow American, Something deeply troubling is happening in America, and it’s happening faster than most people realize. Last year, New York City’s socialist mayor said he wanted to replace what he called **“the frigidity of rugged individualism” with “the warmth of collectivism.”** Then I read that a senior official in that same administration argued that private property is a tool of **oppression**. Those statements are troubling enough. But what really stopped me in my tracks was hearing a popular socialist podcaster tell his audience to **“Kill... landlords... Let the streets soak in their...****capitalist blood.****”** How on earth did ideas like these become acceptable, even helping far-Left candidates to win elections from coast to coast? If you’ve found yourself asking the same question, **[I’d like to send you a FREE copy of _Champions of Freedom: Volume 48_ on the dangers of socialism from Hillsdale College.](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcuK3DAQRb9G3tlI5YfcCy-SeDoM9PSQdEKWRpbKdoFeWHLP74eGnnxAtlWHqsO9f96mN0WW_HpVDgdKaTLBTB-bypTMTnfya95wp4RhSUFPwKErBS-FnJTOdMepUYUZWhD90hc4CHkCqPtWdsU2nBCEPM0aoRXGiL4_ybnBBuYWEJZTXdDwuCe4kAI4tE2lGiPVDFzprlXLzFnDj2hUxop8IoNJhxBjsJRJpyrsa2GHLeeYWP2FwZnBmfwSqo2sTUZZrNAcDM56Uy5S8KkMS7nsiCa48h7s4bBselafE64Off4WDLJ65LwT8sqhgct4Gd_Hl5cbg-7Ibkrh2PUDiXtIEXUmvz5XDg0djtUjOkX2OdTKRUWrZ_X4zyEsT4NPJviMPrN6_PXz_ffXy-v1-_RDlq-3W_mZTrEPJn6QtZQ6yRq-Pl5UOrgi_29n9wH-BgAA___YZakL)** In this collection of speeches, Christopher Caldwell, Kimberley Strassel, John Steele Gordon and others explain where socialism came from, why it has failed everywhere it has been tried, and why it continues to attract support today. **You can claim your free e-book using the secure link below.** | | [Download Your Free Copy](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcuK3DAQRb9G3tlI5YfcCy-SeDoM9PSQdEKWRpbKdoFeWHLP74eGnnxAtlWHqsO9f96mN0WW_HpVDgdKaTLBTB-bypTMTnfya95wp4RhSUFPwKErBS-FnJTOdMepUYUZWhD90hc4CHkCqPtWdsU2nBCEPM0aoRXGiL4_ybnBBuYWEJZTXdDwuCe4kAI4tE2lGiPVDFzprlXLzFnDj2hUxop8IoNJhxBjsJRJpyrsa2GHLeeYWP2FwZnBmfwSqo2sTUZZrNAcDM56Uy5S8KkMS7nsiCa48h7s4bBselafE64Off4WDLJ65LwT8sqhgct4Gd_Hl5cbg-7Ibkrh2PUDiXtIEXUmvz5XDg0djtUjOkX2OdTKRUWrZ_X4zyEsT4NPJviMPrN6_PXz_ffXy-v1-_RDlq-3W_mZTrEPJn6QtZQ6yRq-Pl5UOrgi_29n9wH-BgAA___YZakL)

When Americans lose sight of the principles of individual liberty, constitutional government, and private property, freedom itself becomes vulnerable.
Fortunately, the opposite is also true.
**When citizens understand those principles, they are better prepared to defend them.**
That’s why Hillsdale remains committed to educating all Americans who wish to learn about the principles of liberty—and why generous friends make resources like this available to you free of charge.
**The rise of socialism threatens American liberty, but education is the key to defeating it.**

Pearson stands for a photo with supporters at Campbell Chapel M.B. Church in Bolivar, Tennessee, on September 19, 2026. Photo by Brad Vest/MLK50.
_Story by Katherine Burgess_
Cherie Marceaux lives in Lawrence County, about three hours from Memphis. She and her husband run an animal rescue with horses, goats, pigs, dogs, ferrets, and more.
Marceaux says she's not a Democrat or a Republican, but she knows who she wants to vote for in Tennessee's newly redrawn 9th Congressional District: Memphis Democrat and State Rep. Justin J. Pearson.
In 2023 Pearson was expelled by Republicans from the state legislature as part of a protest for tighter gun safety laws with the "Tennessee Three." Instead of silencing his cause, the expulsion drew national attention and rallied Memphians around his leadership.
When Tennessee Republicans redrew congressional district lines in May, they intended to make District 9 a safe Republican seat. In response, Pearson has focused on issues that appeal to urban and rural voters across the political spectrum: opposition to data centers, gun safety and the economy. And a recent poll has him within striking distance of his Republican opponent, State Sen. Brent Taylor.
"He doesn't just have guts, and he doesn't just call out what's happening, but he's got hope in his eyes. I can see it in his smile. I can see it in his face," Marceaux said. "I don't believe in the party system. I believe in people, and he's a people person. And he's for the environment. How can I not love him?"
_Drop Site 's ongoing collaboration with Barn Raiser [puts a focus on rural politics](https://substack.com/redirect/2fa93baf-c40e-4026-95dd-d71dc0404cda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with a newsletter running through November._
[Sign Up Here](https://substack.com/redirect/2fa93baf-c40e-4026-95dd-d71dc0404cda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
It's unclear whether common ground on these issues will translate to victory for Pearson in a district that is now heavily Republican and predominantly white. But regardless of the outcome, Pearson and his supporters say the coalitions they're creating across District 9 are the first steps to rebuilding progressive power in Tennessee.
The new District 9 voted for Donald Trump by [more than](https://substack.com/redirect/c683b6e7-6fb9-4ef7-88fe-57d28185b753?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 20 points in 2024. The Cook Political Report, a nonpartisan election-rating organization, [called](https://substack.com/redirect/4a25c533-198d-4197-84d6-3c91a625286c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the redistricting intended to strip Tennessee of its last Democratic congressperson "a really effective gerrymander."
But Pearson supporters think there's a chance. In September, Pearson trailed Taylor 44% to 48% in a Hart Research poll commissioned by TN Rise PAC and Three Star PAC (both groups that support Pearson).
"The most powerful thing that's going to come out of this campaign--a win, lose or draw--[is] that people are realizing their own power," Pearson told MLK50: Justice Through Journalism in an interview.
"It's been an overwhelming amount of support, overwhelming amount of just love and power building that I think can change the trajectory of Tennessee politics," Pearson said. "I think that's what we're going to see not just after we win, but over the next several years as we continue to build power in these communities. We're going to be on some county commissions, some school boards, some mayors. This momentum isn't stopping."
## Data Centers, Environmental Pollution at Core of Pearson Campaign
Marceaux's home county of Lawrence is very different from Memphis. The county of about 46,000 people is 94% white and largely rural, while Memphis is a majority Black city of [more than 609,000 residents](https://substack.com/redirect/9ad93f4b-2fd6-4699-8030-a18778c1e94d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
But both places are grappling with the rapid growth of data centers and concerns that they'll worsen water, air, and noise pollution. Opposition to data centers is a unifying position across the 15 counties that form District 9. Voters oppose them by a 36-point margin, according to the Hart Research poll.
The Pearson campaign has leveraged that opposition to expand his base of support, stressing that Pearson's record shows he's on the side of the people, not corporations.
Marceaux said Pearson's longstanding opposition to data centers and other industrial polluters gives him credibility as he challenges Taylor, who was an early supporter of Colossus 1 and received [$10,000 in campaign funding](https://substack.com/redirect/58f75b1c-0620-44f6-8f1a-9b0de4f5eb48?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from a political action committee associated with SpaceXAI.
After a 2025 public hearing regarding the data center's gas turbine permits, Taylor [posted](https://substack.com/redirect/8154e0e8-b56e-427f-80d6-ad9521e1dbe5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X, "I believe our community will unite to embrace this transformative opportunity."
In 2025, Taylor [passed a bill](https://substack.com/redirect/1a73f6cd-d3a2-4234-8e41-533c5cc58f47?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) barring municipalities and utility companies from paying for new electrical infrastructure built to serve a data center. He argued that [the bill would force](https://substack.com/redirect/1ceda893-740b-4f24-b7bc-45e772d2904f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) data centers to pay for their own energy infrastructure, but [critics say](https://substack.com/redirect/bb866201-8ded-4b79-a6df-25c17ee76384?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the law contains a loophole that allows the construction of unregulated gas-fired power plants.
Taylor's campaign did not respond to multiple requests for an interview.
Just 45 days before the election, Pearson spoke in a small church in the town of Bolivar, just over an hour outside Memphis. The [town](https://substack.com/redirect/38658cd4-967f-45cc-8aa9-bf9c507c764a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has just 5,000 residents, about 64% of whom are Black.
"We know we need to stop these toxic data centers from being built in our communities," he told the room, adding that 67% of future data centers are planned in rural America "in order to replace our jobs."
Pearson told the room that this fight is personal: He lives three miles from Colossus 1, the first data center built by Elon Musk's SpaceXAI in the Memphis area.
"People are either worried about the data center that's currently in their backyard if you're in Whitehaven, or they're worried about what could be coming to them if you're in Lawrenceburg," Pearson said in an interview.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e157cbd7-5aa3-4152-b4f4-f1c0379a73fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A protest sign near the site of a proposed data center in Lawrenceburg, Tennessee. Photo by Madison Thorn/MLK50.
Bolivar resident Wanda Robinson said she's hopeful that focusing on data centers will help Pearson overcome the challenges of running in a whiter, more Republican district.
"If we don't speak out against [data centers], they're liable to do anything," Robinson said. "Next thing you know, it may be at our back door. So we have to stand, speak truth to power."
Pearson has launched two advertisements in the greater Nashville area. Both mention data centers: "Now I'm running for Congress to stop data centers from invading our state," he says in one about how his parents taught him "[The Golden Rule](https://substack.com/redirect/0fb66412-6a76-43e1-ad71-058714170b3c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)."
In the [second](https://substack.com/redirect/eb2384e1-96bf-4ced-867c-96b70e2286b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Pearson says, "career politicians and the billionaires who control them want to convince us that the problem is each other: white folk or Black folk, city folk or country folk. Because as long as we're questioning our neighbors, we're not asking the questions that matter."
"Why can't working families afford healthcare or groceries?" he asks. "And why ... are data centers being built in our backyards?"
Taylor's first [campaign advertisement](https://substack.com/redirect/ee60746d-2f16-4ce4-94dd-5457dddad1f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) focuses on how he's "tired of violent criminals running around Tennessee like squirrels in a bait shop."
Back in Lawrence County, Marceaux worries about a [data center](https://substack.com/redirect/08379611-a424-4b18-8555-d9f1c98e48d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) planned for a property near her home. She is concerned about the creek that runs near the data center's planned location, the well water everyone in the area drinks and the swimming hole her grandchildren use. She also worries about the potential impact on the bald eagles and a protected species of heron found in the county. Previously, industries stripped a nearby property of pine trees, she says, leading to a loss of woodpeckers.
"My hope [is] that [Pearson] can get up there and, on a higher level, he can get us some protection, since our local governments don't want to protect us," she said.
## Gun Control, Affordability Cut Across Partisan Divisions
On a sunny Saturday in the town of Savannah, a group of six gathered underneath the town gazebo before heading out to knock on doors across Hardin County.
Kristina Richardson, volunteer lead for the county, said she first became aware of Pearson when he was [temporarily expelled](https://substack.com/redirect/990b6d3d-14cb-4ee0-97b1-c1fc2938cf8b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from the state legislature during the Covenant School protest. A disabled veteran, she said she and her husband "are very pro-Second Amendment," but want "commonsense gun laws." Pearson's protest impressed her, she said.
Most Tennesseans--including Democrats, Republicans and a majority of self-described "MAGA Republicans"--support tougher background checks for firearm owners, according to a [2023 Vanderbilt University poll](https://substack.com/redirect/7b1a1364-4ece-4b38-a9ea-6a8e953c246c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Pearson supporters across District 9 say his focus on gun control and affordability has helped him broaden his appeal to more conservative voters.
Jenna Gammill, who grew up in Savannah and now lives in the adjacent Wayne County, said the area is "bleeding red."
"Slowly but surely, there's people getting fed up, but they don't want to crush their own ego and admit that they messed up," she said. "I'm hoping that they'll maybe start to vote for things that will help them and not harm them."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/203325c9-de79-46cb-97d1-bd10af3a3218?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Audience members at a Pearson rally in the Campbell Chapel M.B. Church in Bolivar, Tennessee, on September 19, 2026. Photo by Brad Vest/MLK50.
Major issues include the lack of access to healthcare and the high cost of diesel fuel for farmers, she said. She thinks more people will vote Democrat in this election--even if they won't say so publicly.
Allie Stokes, who joined Richardson and Gammill to canvas, said when Pearson visited Savannah in June, she heard him answer questions about environmental concerns related to the Tennessee River, which flows through the town of [fewer than 8,000 people](https://substack.com/redirect/edfcbd2f-76c1-450f-b826-2aa3fdce4af0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
"We can't even eat the fish out of the river here safely anymore on a regular basis, because there are signs at the river that say it gives you cancer," Stokes said.
When someone brought that concern up to Pearson, he promised to look into it, she said. He also seemed in touch with people struggling with the cost of living, she said.
"I feel like he's going to be a representative that doesn't forget the people that put him there when he gets in office," she said.
As the group knocked on doors around Hardin County, Stokes voiced surprise at how many Democrat-voting households she saw.
"I'm really passionate about Justin's campaign," Stokes said. "I've seen him speak, and it really seems like he cares about each part of the district that he wants to represent, not just one demographic or one side of it."
## Pearson Supporters Say Coalition-Building Will Outlast Election
Now, Richardson is not only volunteering for Pearson's campaign, but also joining a coalition of people from across the new District 9 who plan to support their neighbors in times of need and advocate for progressive causes even after the election.
Richardson sees some irony in it: Republicans meant to divide up Democrats in creating the new District 9, but instead people are organizing across the 15 counties. "And we're willing to drive," she said.
Regardless of the outcome of this election, "I think [Pearson has] shown us that we do have the power, even though they tried to take it by gerrymandering the district," she said. "It's backfired on them, and it's brought us closer together. It's got me talking to people two, three hours away from me and working with them on this campaign, for instance, but also on other things like the data center in Lawrenceburg."
Pearson said in an interview that as he's traveled the district, he's found more commonality than differences, including among people who vote Independent or Republican.
"It was a concern of mine that folks may not be as receptive to us: that the racism that the state house was banking on, quite frankly, by rigging the district this way would disadvantage us to the point where it'd be impossible. But that's not what we're seeing," Pearson said. "I think our message is reaching Republicans and conservative people because it is people-first policies, and for anybody with a good conscience or goodwill, I think that resonates."

Instead of silencing his cause, the expulsion drew national attention and rallied Memphians around his leadership. Data Centers, Environmental Pollution at Core of Pearson Campaign Marceaux's home county of Lawrence is very different from Memphis. The county of about 46,000 people is 94% white and largely rural, while Memphis is a majority Black city of . body:
Not everyone is paying attention to state-level races. You’re different, Peter

---
Peter, it’s Barack. More people should be paying attention to the key state-level elections on the ballot this November. Because with so much at stake, _it's hard to overstate the importance of these races to the future of our country_. That’s because leaders at the state level oversee elections. They draw the maps for Congress and state legislatures. They make decisions that ultimately make it easier (or harder) to vote. And with free and fair elections under attack — from mid-decade gerrymandering and threats of voter suppression — we need more state-level officials who care about building a stronger democracy. The National Democratic Redistricting Committee, which I co-founded with Attorney General Eric Holder, fights alongside its affiliates to elect state lawmakers and governors who are on the side of the people — who believe in fair maps and fair access to the ballot. The NDRC also fights to elect fair-minded judges who won’t bend the law or twist the rules of our democracy to help out a political party. **[The NDRC needs your help. They’ve endorsed over 300 Democracy Defenders who are up for election in 19 days in over a dozen states across the country. Hi Peter, it’s Jon Ossoff.
Five years ago, Georgia sent the young Jewish son of an immigrant and a Black pastor who holds Dr. King's pulpit at Ebenezer Baptist Church to the U.S. Senate — winning the Senate majority for Democrats.
And this year, our country is counting on us to win here again. Because only by regaining Congressional power can we stop the chaos and corruption of the Trump administration.
So if you’re ready to stop MAGA and restore checks and balances, please chip in what you can to support my campaign here in Georgia.
**Here’s the link to donate:[https://act.electjon.com/go/donate](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-oct26.FRbHBd&refcode=em261017-1-f&utm_campaign=em261017-1-f&t=2&akid=3104%2E5691347%2EoFCNCi)**
Otherwise, let me remind you why I ran for the Senate — and why these midterm elections are even more urgent.
Before I was elected, I led investigations of corruption and human rights abuses worldwide. We exposed wrongdoing in countries where criticizing the government is dangerous, where whistleblowers and witnesses will only meet in secret, where protest carries the risk of prosecution.
More and more, Trump's rule reminds me of those places where dissent was silenced by intimidation.
I ran for Senate in Georgia because I saw the danger in electing someone so profoundly unfit for the presidency, and to confront the corruption that made his rise possible. We defeated him, and I won.
But now, this President is staging a power grab unprecedented in our history. This President has:
* Tried to jail elected leaders of the opposition and prosecute Americans who have defied or criticized him.

* Allowed masked federal agents to kick down Americans’ doors without so much as a warrant from a judge, assault and even kill Americans with apparent license from the very top.

* Used the office of the Presidency to enrich his family in a way we have never, ever seen in American history.

**This is not a drill, and it’s not a bad dream. As citizens, this moment is the test of our lifetimes.**
The only way to dig ourselves out of this chaos is absolute victory in the midterms.
And just like last time, I can’t do it alone.
So I’m asking:
[**Please, make a contribution to my reelection campaign today, of $5 or any amount that works for you.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-oct26.FRbHBd&refcode=em261017-1-f&utm_campaign=em261017-1-f&t=3&akid=3104%2E5691347%2EoFCNCi)

**Can Republicans Buy Their Way Out of This?**
_Midterm HQ: The GOP is cutting its House losses and spending like mad to hold a couple of Senate races. Will it work? [5 min read]_
## **Toplines for the Week**
The past week brought the whole midterm fight into focus:**it 's the Republican money vs. the Democrats' math.**
The structural picture--the math--tells the same consistent story it has for months: it should be a Democratic blowout. As you can see in the dashboard below, the environment is at _Toxic Avenger_ levels for the GOP.
But Republicans have a plan.
It involves cutting dead weight, keeping things close in a handful of races, and crossing their fingers for a late effect that we've seen before. Will it happen? Let's unpack it.

name: Douglas Carswell
subject: What Mississippi really thinks – Speaker White poll results
body:
Speaker Jason White published a new poll this week. | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/jwpoll?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
Speaker Jason White published a new poll this week. It is worth reading closely. Cygnal surveyed 501 likely Mississippi voters and found that inflation is the top concern (22%), followed by crime (19%), healthcare (15%) and taxes (14%). Seventy-two percent want the ballot initiative restored. Just 8% oppose it. No other question in the poll unites voters like that. Republicans back it 78 to 5, and Democrats 66 to 11. Most voters want to end property tax on their homes: 57% for, 25% against. For homeowners aged 65 and over, support rises to 70%. Asked whether they would rather scrap homestead property tax or car tag fees, voters chose property tax, 51 to 35. And school choice? This is where it gets interesting. When first asked about Magnolia Student Accounts, the program in House Bill 2, voters were in favor, 41 to 39. Then they were told that in other states with school choice, test scores have improved in both public and private schools. Support jumped to 50%. Opposition fell to 27%. A two-point lead became a 23-point lead. One voter in ten moved straight from oppose to support. Given that Mississippi is now surrounded by states with school choice – and the positive effect of parent power is becoming clearer by the day – expect an upswing in support for reform in our state. Public opinion is not fixed. It moves when someone makes the argument. Look at who moved. Women over 55 shifted 41 points. Rural voters shifted 34 points, and so did white voters without a college degree. These are not the people the critics of school choice claim to speak for. They are key voters in our state. By 42 to 24, voters also say they are more likely to back a candidate who supports school choice. HB2 passed the House in January. It was killed by a Senate committee without much discussion. The numbers show which chamber is closer to the voters. On property tax, the message is equally clear. Voters want relief. But asked how to replace the revenue, they split three ways: 35% favor a local sales tax, 29% would raise the state sales tax, and 36% don’t know. The opportunity for anyone offering to channel data center revenue into offsetting property tax bills is there for the taking. Then there is that 72% for the ballot initiative. Voters want a way to act when the Legislature won’t. Read the school choice numbers and the initiative numbers side by side, and it is hard not to see a connection. Speaker White and the House now have the data. The voters have made their view plain. What is needed is the argument, made clearly, often and everywhere. That is precisely what we intend to keep doing.
---
| |
---
Warm regards,

Douglas Carswell
President & CEO
Mississippi Center for Public Policy

We should take over the voting, the voting in at least many – 15 places. The Republicans ought to nationalize the voting.”_**
_\- Trump on a podcast with his former FBI Director, Dan Bongino, in February 2026_

**2)** Then, he lied to the American people about countless claims of voter fraud and thousands of noncitizen voters in our democracy – _despite voter fraud being an ultra-rare occurrence._
| | **_“Our elections [in 2020] were left vulnerable to being rigged and stolen. Evidence of fraud has been buried. Hundreds of thousands of non-citizens... are listed and active on the voter rolls.”_**
_\- Trump in a primetime speech on “election security” in July_

_\- Trump in TIME Magazine in early October_

I have a couple of rules when I'm out on the campaign trail:
1. Talk to every voter possible, whether they're a Democrat, Republican, or Independent.
2. Treat people with respect and really listen.
3. **Pet every dog you can.**

I'm very serious about #3.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/daf5adda-d6bb-447c-b739-1d2d05213910?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[CHIP IN](https://substack.com/redirect/daf5adda-d6bb-447c-b739-1d2d05213910?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I don't think there are a lot of pets at fancy fundraisers, so petting cute dogs is one of many things Dan Meuser is missing out on when he's hiding from the voters.
**The most important thing he 's missing is the chance to hear from the people he's supposed to represent. But he doesn't care about us enough to change that.**
While Dan's anywhere but our part of PA over these final 17 days, I'll be out on the campaign trail, doing what I have been doing this whole time. Showing up.
But we have a lot of ground to cover (and a lot of dogs to pet) before Election Day, and I can't do this without you.
**[Will you chip in to help us keep showing up and flip this seat?](https://substack.com/redirect/daf5adda-d6bb-447c-b739-1d2d05213910?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Thank you,
Rachel Wallace

# Conforti Grassroots Newsletter
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |

**Welcome to the final stretch of our campaign!**
.With the 2026 Midterm Election just weeks away, this interactive grassroots newsletter is your central hub for the final push to bring true representation back to the hardworking constituents of Illinois' 6th Congressional District.
.Our campaign has always been built on a "district-first" mentality, prioritizing your needs through sensible solutions and open dialogue. Now, we need your help to cross the finish line. As we continue to provide you with regular updates on policy, campaign events, and current community events happening right here in our district, your active participation is more critical than ever.
.Please click the button below to make a donation today—your grassroots contributions are what make this possible.
---
| | [DONATE](https://us.list-manage.com/65SWoLoZywe?e=25f4fa3311&c2id=7b058fb5598c3e136d157ed790328086)
---
| |
---
| |
### Special Release.
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | |
## The Conforti Brief
---
| | **Informing voters** on current events and how Niki plans to help them once in office.
---
| |
**Standing With Female Athletes: Condemning Threats and Protecting Title IX****.
** Recently, Fox News and OutKick reported on an alarming and unacceptable incident involving 20-year-old NCAA softball player Kendall Kotzmacher. Because of her public **advocacy against biological males competing in girls' and women's sports** , the Colorado Christian University sophomore revealed that someone threatened to come to her college campus and threatened her life. In addition to the police-investigated death threat, Kotzmacher has endured a barrage of online harassment telling her she does not deserve to live, with online targeting even spreading to her supportive teammates. Her advocacy began after her high school team lost a 2025 state semifinal game to a team featuring a transgender pitcher, and she has since traveled to Capitol Hill—where **Democrat lawmakers largely walked out on or ignored female athletes sharing their stories** —to fight for fairness and safety for the next generation of young women.
.Lawmakers must condemn these vile threats and intimidation tactics against women who are speaking out for their fundamental rights. **No young woman should ever fear for her life, face harassment, or be bullied into silence simply for wanting nothing more than the opportunity to compete on a fair and safe playing field.**
.For decades, female athletes have worked tirelessly to achieve equality in athletics. Protecting these hard-won opportunities is a matter of defending the sanctity of fairness and the important rights owed to women under Title IX. Unfortunately, **incumbent Democrat Sean Casten and his party have threatened the integrity of women’s sports and the foundational protections of Title IX.** Instead of standing up for female athletes and common-sense fairness, Casten is more concerned with partisan messaging and satisfying the most radical elements of his party—pushing a far-left agenda that is directly in opposition with the values of his constituents in Illinois' 6th Congressional District. By refusing to protect biological women’s spaces and sports, Casten and his allies have eroded the very equality Title IX was created to guarantee.
.As your candidate for Illinois' 6th Congressional District, **Niki Conforti maintains a "district-first" mentality and firmly believes that equal opportunities for women mean female athletes deserve to compete on a fair playing field** —without being forced to compete against biological males.
. When elected to represent the 6th District in the U.S. House of Representatives, Niki will take action to protect women's sports, supporting policies like:
.
* **Supporting the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act:** Proudly supporting legislation like S.9, the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act, to prevent biological males from competing against biological females in athletic competitions. This crucial measure provides positive protections and ensures the integrity of women's sports is maintained.
* **Defending the Sanctity of Title IX:** Work to ensure that the important rights owed to women athletes under Title IX of the Education Amendments are fiercely protected from radical partisan overreach.
* **Ensuring Safe and Fair Competition:** Niki will fight to guarantee that every young woman in our district has the chance to compete, excel, and be recognized fairly for her dedication and hard work—free from intimidation and unfair biological disadvantages.
.

Children are our future, and we must protect them. **It is time to stand with brave female athletes across our nation** , demand accountability, and ensure that equality in women's sports is grounded in a fair playing field.
Stay informed on this issue—[**read the full breakdown here.**](https://us.list-manage.com/1132jr0KHrC?e=25f4fa3311&c2id=7b058fb5598c3e136d157ed790328086)
---
|
---
|
---
| | **Key Dates for the 2026 General Election (DuPage County)**
.
* First day to apply for a vote-by-mail ballot: August 5th
* Early voting and vote-by-mail voting begins: September 24th
* Last day to request a vote-by-mail ballot: October 29th
* Last day for early voting: November 2nd
* General Election Day: November 3rd
.

**Key Dates for the 2026 General Election (Cook County)**
**.**
* First day to apply for a vote-by-mail ballot: August 5th
* First day to vote early in Chicago (Downtown Only): September 24th
* Last day for online voter registration: October 18th
* Early voting opens in all 50 city wards and suburban Cook County: October 19th
.
.

**Get out the vote:** whether you plan to vote by mail, early voting in person, or voting in person on election day, it’s important we get out the vote to defeat incumbent Sean Casten.

.
---
|
---
| |

**Call To Action! Show Your Support: Request a Yard Sign Today!
.**As we approach the November 3rd General Election, grassroots engagement is essential to defeating incumbent Sean Casten. You can help spread the word and showcase our "district-first" mentality by **placing a Niki Conforti yard sign in your yard.** Visible community support is a powerful way to show your neighbors that we are united in the fight for economic affordability, community safety, and sensible solutions for the 6th District.
. To request a sign for your home or business, please contact our team at [**info@conforti4congress.com.**](mailto:info@conforti4congress.com?subject=Yard%20Sign%20Request&body=) Strong local momentum is the key to curbing reckless spending and securing a safer future for Illinois families.
.
Let us know you would like a sign, and we will arrange to get one to you right away!
